# The two-tasklet local-mode scenario every core runs, and the output every
# core must release. Read by the Rust SDK, Java and Elixir local-mode suites,
# so the Elixir SDK's own core and `flz_core` are compared against ONE recorded
# expectation rather than by inspection.
#
# The graph is `lines -> Split -> (inter-tasklet, keyed by word) -> Tally ->
# totals sink`, with Tally counting occurrences of the word its Cell is.
#
# `lines` are fed to the entry channel in order. `totals` are the values the
# sink releases, as a MULTISET: one Cell per word, and Cells run
# concurrently, so the order across different words is not a property any core
# has. Per word the order is FIFO, which is why `the 1` precedes `the 2`.
lines: the quick brown fox
lines: the lazy dog
totals: the 1
totals: quick 1
totals: brown 1
totals: fox 1
totals: the 2
totals: lazy 1
totals: dog 1
